2026 Was Our Biggest Year Yet

On October 3, 2026, Team Golomboski took to the path for the Rhode Island Optimism Walk — and this community showed up in a big way.

Our team raised $7,273.75, passing our $7,000 goal and finishing at 103% of goal. Every dollar supports the APDA Rhode Island Chapter and the local families it serves.

Thank you. To every donor who gave, every sponsor who stood with us, and every volunteer and walker who gave their time — this result belongs to all of you.

Home · Our Story

Our Story

A brother and sister turned their father's fight into a promise — and Rhode Island has been keeping it with them since 2014.

How Team Golomboski Began

Team Golomboski was founded in 2014 by siblings Alicia Golomboski and Joseph Golomboski Jr. to honor their father, Joseph P. Golomboski Sr., who was living with Parkinson's disease.

Joseph Sr. was diagnosed with early-onset Parkinson's at age 44. His children watched what the disease takes — and decided to answer it the way their family answers everything: together, and out loud. The team they built walks and fundraises for the APDA Rhode Island Chapter, so that other Rhode Island families facing Parkinson's have programs, support, and a community to lean on.

What started as one family's walk team has grown into twelve years of fundraising, events, and community support — and leadership of the chapter itself. But the heart of it has never changed: this is a family honoring its dad.

In Loving Memory

Joseph P. Golomboski Sr.

1959 – 2019

Diagnosed with early-onset Parkinson's disease at 44, Joseph Sr. faced the disease with the same strength his family now walks with. He passed away on August 9, 2019, at Cherry Hill Manor. Every step Team Golomboski takes is taken in his name.

What We Stand For

Five values have carried this team from its first walk in 2014 to today.

Family

Where this team started — a brother and sister walking for their dad — and still who we are.

Compassion

Parkinson's touches whole families. We show up for all of them, not just on walk day.

Community

Rhode Island is small and mighty. Our neighbors, sponsors, and volunteers make every result possible.

Perseverance

Twelve years in, we are still walking — because the need hasn't gone away, and neither have we.

Creativity

Concerts, comedy nights, and community drives — if it brings people together for the cause, we'll try it.

What Is Parkinson's Disease?

Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurological disorder that affects movement. It develops when the brain cells that produce dopamine — a chemical that helps coordinate smooth, purposeful movement — become impaired or die. As dopamine declines, movement symptoms appear and gradually change over time.

There is no cure yet, but treatments, exercise, and support can make a real difference in daily life — which is exactly why the APDA exists, and why Team Golomboski fundraises for its Rhode Island Chapter. The education below follows APDA's published resources; the full library lives at apdaparkinson.org.

Motor Symptoms

The movement symptoms most associated with Parkinson's:

  • Tremor — often beginning in a hand, especially at rest
  • Slowness of movement (bradykinesia) — everyday tasks take longer
  • Stiffness and rigidity — in the limbs, neck, or trunk
  • Balance and posture problems — raising the risk of falls

Non-Motor Symptoms

Parkinson's reaches well beyond movement — these symptoms can appear early:

  • Reduced sense of smell
  • Sleep problems, including acting out dreams
  • Depression and anxiety
  • Cognitive changes and slowed thinking
  • Fatigue and digestive issues such as constipation

Young-Onset Parkinson's

When Parkinson's is diagnosed before age 50, it's called young-onset Parkinson's disease. It often progresses more slowly, but it arrives in the middle of careers and raising families — a different set of challenges that calls for its own support.

It's personal for this team: Joseph Golomboski Sr. was diagnosed at age 44. Read our story.

Help Right Here in Rhode Island

Through the APDA Rhode Island Chapter, local families can connect with:

  • Support groups across Rhode Island
  • Rock Steady Boxing and other exercise programs
  • Exercise & wellness programs built for people with Parkinson's
  • The APDA helpline and chapter staff who know the local landscape

Start at the chapter's home on the web: apdaparkinson.org

This page is educational information drawn from APDA resources — it isn't medical advice. Anyone with questions about symptoms or treatment should talk with their own doctor or neurologist.

Turn Understanding Into Support

The programs listed above run on community support. A gift to APDA Rhode Island keeps them going for the next family that needs them.

Stories From Our Community

Standing Strong Through COVID

In the spring and summer of 2020, with the community hurting, Team Golomboski turned its fundraising energy toward neighbors in need.

April 2020
$113.30

For the RI Community Food Bank

Team Golomboski raised and donated $113.30 to the Rhode Island Community Food Bank, helping keep shelves stocked for Rhode Island families during the first hard months of the pandemic.

April 2020
8 XL pizzas

Dinner for the Cherry Hill Manor Team

The team delivered 8 extra-large pizzas to the staff at Cherry Hill Manor — a thank-you to the caregivers who looked after residents, including families like ours, when it mattered most.

July 2020
Potter League

For the Animals, Too

The giving extended to four-legged Rhode Islanders: Team Golomboski made a donation to the Potter League for Animals, supporting the shelter's care for animals waiting on their forever homes.

Press Kit

About Team Golomboski

Boilerplate — please feel free to use as written.

Team Golomboski is a family-led fundraising team based in Warwick, Rhode Island, founded in 2014 by siblings Joseph Golomboski Jr. and Alicia Golomboski in memory of their father, Joseph P. Golomboski Sr., who was diagnosed with early-onset Parkinson's disease at age 44 and passed away in 2019. The team supports the Rhode Island Chapter of the American Parkinson Disease Association (APDA) and has raised over $20,000 since 2014 for local programs, support services, exercise and wellness programs, and research toward a cure.

Key Stats

  • 2014 Founded in Warwick, Rhode Island
  • $20,000+ Raised for APDA Rhode Island since 2014
  • 12 years Active in the Rhode Island Optimism Walk
  • $7,273.75 Raised by the team in 2026
  • 103% Of the team's $7,000 goal in 2026
  • Oct 3, 2026 Most recent Rhode Island Optimism Walk & 5K
